_note: Every tunable number in the game. If a number appears in a .js file, it belongs here instead. Changing anything under 'climate', 'player.speed', or any site x/z means re-running the balance check.

world._scaleNote: One number for the size of the whole world. 1 is the original 3400 m map; 0.55 shrinks it to about 1870 m across, which puts the same seventeen places closer together without moving any of them relative to each other. Everything measured in metres multiplies by this at load — sites, camps, graves, the dawn line and its speed, the grass band, the herd. Terrain detail gets finer at the same rate so the hills stay the same size relative to the map. Deliberately NOT scaled: how fast you walk, and how close you must stand to survey something — you are the same size whatever the world does.

palette._note: Ground colour, baked into the terrain mesh once at load. Costs nothing at runtime — change these freely. Each triple is r,g,b in 0..1. 'ash' is the flat ground, 'rock' is what steep slopes show, 'broadWarm' drifts the tone slowly across the map so large areas are not one flat colour.

sky._note: The sky gradient, baked into the sky shader at load. Triples are r,g,b in 0..1. 'haze' should stay close to render.fogColour — that match is what makes the ground fade into the sky instead of ending at a visible line. 'dither' hides banding in the gradient on 8-bit screens; set it to 0 to switch that off.

climate._note: The whole clock. dawn0 is where the dawn line starts in metres; dawnVelocity is metres per second. lethal is the temperature that kills a site. A site at x becomes lost at (x + (lethal + 12) / k - dawn0) / dawnVelocity seconds.

gait._note: The elbow base bend of 0.30 rad is load-bearing. A straight arm reads as a robot. gait.test.js asserts it never goes below this.

colour._note: Blade colour. 'tint' is the per-blade base (multiplied by a random 0.72-1.22 so no two blades match); 'root' is what the bottom of each blade is multiplied by, which is what gives the band depth instead of reading as flat green paper. 'rootHeight' is how far up the blade the root colour has faded out (0..1).

ashwaiters._note: Currently a damage radius, not a creature. Known issue 2 in HANDOFF.

sites._note: The six findings. Prose for each lives in story.json under the same id. duration is seconds of holding still to complete the survey.

camps._note: The Meridian chain. Each camp is further north than the last. 'gives' names the site it answers from their archive, or null.

graves._note: Never marked on the compass or the chart. Finding them is the discovery.

shelter._note: The sixth camp. Only appears on the compass after camp five is read, and then only as '?'.

textures._note: Every texture is drawn in code at load — there are no image files. Sizes are pixels per side: a 512 map costs about 1.4 MB on the graphics card, a 256 map about 350 KB. If the game runs slowly it halves all of these automatically (render.downgrade.textureScale) and redraws them. Setting 'enabled' false turns every generated map off and falls back to plain colours.

audio._note: Everything you hear is made from filtered noise at run time — there are no sound files. Gains are 0..1 and they add up, so raising several at once is how you get distortion. The wind is meant to sit under everything and only be noticed when it stops. Mute is V.

smoothing._note: Seconds for a level to travel most of the way to its target. Small is twitchy, large is syrupy. 'null' is deliberately quicker than the rest — the silence should arrive faster than it leaves.

wind._note: The floor. 'gain' is the level on flat, cool ground; elevation and heat add to it. Gusts are two slow sines beating against each other so the bed never loops audibly.

herd._note: Low-passed noise, panned by the same bearing the soundfield strip draws. 'curve' above 1 keeps it felt rather than heard until you are close: at half range it is a quarter as loud. Range itself comes from striders.audibleRange.

foot._note: One burst per footfall, fired off the gait phase so it lands with the foot rather than on a timer. 1.3g is in these numbers: low filter, slow decay, weight. 'phaseOffset' slides the hit earlier or later in the stride.

null._note: The ashwaiter silence. At full null everything is multiplied by zero — actual silence, not a quiet mix. 'curve' above 1 makes the drop bite earlier as you approach the den.

render._lightNote: One warm key (the fixed low sun) and two cool fills. Keeping the key warm and the fills cool is what gives the ground shape; making them the same colour flattens it.

downgrade._note: Keep this path working. Target is 60fps on integrated graphics.
